de.settingsHelpAntiAliasing: Smooths the edges of rotated and scaled layers. Saved in the project, and the same for the preview and the export.
de.settingsHelpAntiAliasingInUse: This graphics card does not offer the setting above, so Lumit is using the highest it does. The project is unchanged.
de.settingsHelpAutomaticUpdates: Look for a new version of Lumit when it starts, at most once a day. Nothing is downloaded until you ask for it.
de.settingsHelpCacheBudget: How much memory finished frames may hold, of the {total} this machine has.
de.settingsHelpCacheInUse: {hits} of {requests} frames were served from the cache; {decodes} were decoded.
de.settingsHelpChromeLabels: Whether buttons, tabs and toggles show their word or the glyph that stands for it. Hover text always says the word, whichever you choose, and anything you typed yourself is never turned into a picture.
de.settingsHelpColourScheme: The palette every panel draws from.
de.settingsHelpCompact: Draw rows a little tighter, so more of a layer stack and more parameters fit on screen. Nothing else changes.
de.settingsHelpCorners: How rounded controls and panels are.
de.settingsHelpCustomColours: Start from this scheme and set any colour yourself.
de.settingsHelpDiskBudget: How much disk space parked frames may take. These survive closing Lumit, so a project reopens warm.
de.settingsHelpFramesWaitingToBeWritten: The write-behind queue to the disk cache, which is bounded at eight frames.
de.settingsHelpGraphicsMemoryReserved: What the driver has taken from the system for those, and how much of it is in use. The gap is memory Lumit has released and the driver has not handed back.
de.settingsHelpHeldByTheGraphicsDriver: Pictures and buffers the driver still has for Lumit. A handful is normal — the frames on the card, the ones being made. Thousands means pictures the engine finished with were never destroyed, and on a Mac that memory is inside the total above.
de.settingsHelpInterfaceScale: How large every panel draws, for a dense or a distant screen.
de.settingsHelpInUse: Frames held on the card, ready to show without compositing.
de.settingsHelpInUse2: Frames on disk, one promotion away from playing.
de.settingsHelpLanguage: What Lumit is written in. Translations come from volunteers, so a new language may be part English at first.
de.settingsHelpMotion: How much controls animate as they change.
de.settingsHelpNotHeldByAnyCache: The process, less every store above that is inside it — which on this machine includes the frames on the card. A large number here is not a cache to shrink: it is memory nothing in this window is counting, and it is worth reporting.
de.settingsHelpNowhereToPark: Nowhere: this machine has no folder Lumit may write to.
de.settingsHelpOpenMediaDecoders: One per footage item in play. Each holds buffers of its own that no budget here covers.
de.settingsHelpPanelLayout: Return every panel to its default place and size.
de.settingsHelpPasteLayersAtTheirOriginal: A pasted layer keeps the timecode it was copied at, instead of starting at the playhead. For rebuilding the same moment in a second composition; leave it off for the everyday "put one here". Effects always paste with their first keyframe at the playhead, whichever way this is set.
de.settingsHelpPlayheadStaysWherePlaybackSt: Leave the playhead on the frame that was on screen when playback stopped, instead of putting it back where playing started. Dragging the ruler while playing always stops and follows the pointer, whichever way this is set.
de.settingsHelpQualityTier: What the realtime controller has settled on.
de.settingsHelpRetimeOpensToVelocity: The Retime graph opens showing playback speed per cent — one point per keyframe, dragged up to speed up and below zero to reverse — instead of which moment of the source is showing.
de.settingsHelpRetimeValuesInSeconds: The Retime row shows which moment of the source is playing as a number of seconds, instead of as a timecode in the same HH:MM:SS:FF form as every other time in the editor. Seconds can say a position between two frames; a timecode cannot.
de.settingsHelpScopeEverywhere: Every project that has not been given a place of its own.
de.settingsHelpScopeThisProject: Saved inside this project, so it travels with a copy of it.
de.settingsHelpShowTheToneMapButton: Put the tone map button on the Viewer bar. Tone mapping folds a picture brighter than the screen can show back into what it can, so the detail up there can be seen while you work — it is a way of looking, and it never reaches an export. Off unless you ask for it.
de.settingsHelpSmoothThePictureWhenZoomed: Off, a pixel magnified past 1:1 stays a square, which is what you zoom in to see. On, the picture is blended between pixels — softer, and easier on the eye when the zoom is for framing rather than for inspecting.
de.settingsHelpSurroundTakesThemeColours: Off, the area around the picture is a neutral grey — a grade cannot be judged against a tinted surround. On, it matches the rest of the shell.
de.settingsHelpThisProcess: What the system says Lumit is holding, all in — the number Activity Monitor and Task Manager show.
de.settingsHelpTransformInEffectControls: Repeat the layer's Transform rows above its effects. The Timeline already shows them when a layer is twirled open.
de.settingsHelpVideoArrivesAsASequence: Video and image sequences added to a composition become a Sequence layer, which can be cut into clips on its own row. Still images are never wrapped.
de.settingsHelpVramBudget: How much video memory finished frames may hold, of the {total} on the card.
de.settingsHelpWaveformsRiseFromTheBottom: A waveform stands on the floor of its row instead of being centred about silence, each column reaching up by how far the sound swung either way. Half of a centred wave is a mirror of the other half, so this spends the whole row on the half that says something — useful in a short row. Applies to the single wave and the frequency stack alike.
de.settingsHelpWaveformsShowTheFrequencySta: A layer's waveform draws as three stacked waves — bass, middle and treble — instead of one. A loud passage is a solid block on a single wave whichever instrument is playing; the stack shows the kick apart from the hats, so a cut can be aimed at either. Turn it off for one plain wave.
de.settingsHelpWhenTheMachineCannotKeep: Adaptive keeps time and softens the picture; every frame keeps the picture and takes the time it needs.
de.settingsPasteLayersAtTheirOriginal: Paste layers at their original time
de.settingsSmoothThePictureWhenZoomed: Smooth the picture when zoomed in
de.settingsVideoArrivesAsASequence: Video arrives as a Sequence layer
de.settingsWhenTheMachineCannotKeep: When the machine cannot keep up

de.tokenAccentHelp: The one accent: focus, the playhead, what is chosen.
de.tokenAccenthoverHelp: The accent with the pointer on it.
de.tokenAnimatedHelp: Keyframes, the stopwatch when it is on, a handle or value field in hand, and the work-area band.
de.tokenCachediskHelp: The disk tier of the Timeline's cache bar.
de.tokenCurveHelp: A property's stroke in the graph editor.
de.tokenHairlineHelp: The line between rows and panels.
de.tokenHairlinestrongHelp: The same line where it has to carry more weight.
de.tokenMarkerHelp: Comp markers on the time ruler, and the box holding what one says. A grey by default — a marker says *here*, not *careful*.
de.tokenSelectionfillHelp: Under a selected layer or property; half as strong under a highlighted one.
de.tokenSuccessHelp: Something finished, or held in the cache.
de.tokenSurface0Help: The deepest ground — behind panels, and the app backdrop.
de.tokenSurface1Help: A panel's own ground, and the Timeline inside the work area.
de.tokenSurface2Help: Rows and cards lifted off the panel.
de.tokenSurface3Help: A field or button at rest.
de.tokenSurface4Help: The same, with the pointer over it.
de.tokenTextdisabledHelp: A control that cannot be used right now.
de.tokenTextmutedHelp: Hints and the lines under a setting.
de.tokenTextprimaryHelp: Names, values, anything you read first.
de.tokenTimelineoutofrangeHelp: The Timeline's ground either side of the work area, so the part you are delivering reads apart from the rest.
de.tokenWarningHelp: Something worth reading before carrying on.
de.tokenWaveformhighHelp: The top band — hats, sibilance, transient edge.
de.tokenWaveformlowHelp: The bottom band of the multiwave stack — kicks and bass.
de.tokenWaveformmidHelp: The middle band — most of a voice, a snare's body.
de.tokenWaveformrestHelp: The single wave a layer or a clip draws. Content, not state — never the accent.

zh.settingsHelpGraphicsMemoryReserved: What the driver has taken from the system for those, and how much of it is in use. The gap is memory Lumit has released and the driver has not handed back.
zh.settingsHelpHeldByTheGraphicsDriver: Pictures and buffers the driver still has for Lumit. A handful is normal — the frames on the card, the ones being made. Thousands means pictures the engine finished with were never destroyed, and on a Mac that memory is inside the total above.
zh.settingsHelpInterfaceScale: How large every panel draws, for a dense or a distant screen.
zh.settingsHelpInUse: Frames held on the card, ready to show without compositing.
zh.settingsHelpInUse2: Frames on disk, one promotion away from playing.
zh.settingsHelpLanguage: What Lumit is written in. Translations come from volunteers, so a new language may be part English at first.
zh.settingsHelpMotion: How much controls animate as they change.
zh.settingsHelpNotHeldByAnyCache: The process, less every store above that is inside it — which on this machine includes the frames on the card. A large number here is not a cache to shrink: it is memory nothing in this window is counting, and it is worth reporting.
zh.settingsHelpNowhereToPark: Nowhere: this machine has no folder Lumit may write to.
zh.settingsHelpOpenMediaDecoders: One per footage item in play. Each holds buffers of its own that no budget here covers.
zh.settingsHelpPanelLayout: Return every panel to its default place and size.
zh.settingsHelpPasteLayersAtTheirOriginal: A pasted layer keeps the timecode it was copied at, instead of starting at the playhead. For rebuilding the same moment in a second composition; leave it off for the everyday "put one here". Effects always paste with their first keyframe at the playhead, whichever way this is set.
zh.settingsHelpPlayheadStaysWherePlaybackSt: Leave the playhead on the frame that was on screen when playback stopped, instead of putting it back where playing started. Dragging the ruler while playing always stops and follows the pointer, whichever way this is set.
zh.settingsHelpQualityTier: What the realtime controller has settled on.
zh.settingsHelpRetimeOpensToVelocity: The Retime graph opens showing playback speed per cent — one point per keyframe, dragged up to speed up and below zero to reverse — instead of which moment of the source is showing.
zh.settingsHelpRetimeValuesInSeconds: The Retime row shows which moment of the source is playing as a number of seconds, instead of as a timecode in the same HH:MM:SS:FF form as every other time in the editor. Seconds can say a position between two frames; a timecode cannot.
zh.settingsHelpScopeEverywhere: Every project that has not been given a place of its own.
zh.settingsHelpScopeThisProject: Saved inside this project, so it travels with a copy of it.
zh.settingsHelpShapeEasesInAPopup: The graph editor's Easing button opens the shape editor in a small floating box instead of the Easing panel. The box closes whenever you click outside it — and choosing different keyframes is a click outside — so one drawn shape can only be tried on the selection that was live when it opened. Turn it on to save the screen space.
zh.settingsHelpShowTheToneMapButton: Put the tone map button on the Viewer bar. Tone mapping folds a picture brighter than the screen can show back into what it can, so the detail up there can be seen while you work — it is a way of looking, and it never reaches an export. Off unless you ask for it.
zh.settingsHelpSmoothThePictureWhenZoomed: Off, a pixel magnified past 1:1 stays a square, which is what you zoom in to see. On, the picture is blended between pixels — softer, and easier on the eye when the zoom is for framing rather than for inspecting.
zh.settingsHelpSurroundTakesThemeColours: Off, the area around the picture is a neutral grey — a grade cannot be judged against a tinted surround. On, it matches the rest of the shell.
zh.settingsHelpThisProcess: What the system says Lumit is holding, all in — the number Activity Monitor and Task Manager show.
zh.settingsHelpTransformInEffectControls: Repeat the layer's Transform rows above its effects. The Timeline already shows them when a layer is twirled open.
zh.settingsHelpUseThemeColours: Off, a scope reads on the standard near-black graticule whatever the chrome — which is how a signal is measured. On, it takes the theme's colours instead.
zh.settingsHelpVideoArrivesAsASequence: Video and image sequences added to a composition become a Sequence layer, which can be cut into clips on its own row. Still images are never wrapped.
zh.settingsHelpVramBudget: How much video memory finished frames may hold, of the {total} on the card.
zh.settingsHelpWaveformsRiseFromTheBottom: A waveform stands on the floor of its row instead of being centred about silence, each column reaching up by how far the sound swung either way. Half of a centred wave is a mirror of the other half, so this spends the whole row on the half that says something — useful in a short row. Applies to the single wave and the frequency stack alike.
zh.settingsHelpWaveformsShowTheFrequencySta: A layer's waveform draws as three stacked waves — bass, middle and treble — instead of one. A loud passage is a solid block on a single wave whichever instrument is playing; the stack shows the kick apart from the hats, so a cut can be aimed at either. Turn it off for one plain wave.
zh.settingsHelpWhenTheMachineCannotKeep: Adaptive keeps time and softens the picture; every frame keeps the picture and takes the time it needs.
zh.settingsHelpYourThemes: Duplicate one to change it without losing the original, or send one to somebody as a file.

zh_Hant.settingsHelpCacheBudget: How much memory finished frames may hold, of the {total} this machine has.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpCacheInUse: {hits} of {requests} frames were served from the cache; {decodes} were decoded.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpChromeLabels: Whether buttons, tabs and toggles show their word or the glyph that stands for it. Hover text always says the word, whichever you choose, and anything you typed yourself is never turned into a picture.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpColourScheme: The palette every panel draws from.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpCompact: Draw rows a little tighter, so more of a layer stack and more parameters fit on screen. Nothing else changes.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpCorners: How rounded controls and panels are.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpCustomColours: Start from this scheme and set any colour yourself.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpDiskBudget: How much disk space parked frames may take. These survive closing Lumit, so a project reopens warm.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpFramesWaitingToBeWritten: The write-behind queue to the disk cache, which is bounded at eight frames.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpGraphicsMemoryReserved: What the driver has taken from the system for those, and how much of it is in use. The gap is memory Lumit has released and the driver has not handed back.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpHeldByTheGraphicsDriver: Pictures and buffers the driver still has for Lumit. A handful is normal — the frames on the card, the ones being made. Thousands means pictures the engine finished with were never destroyed, and on a Mac that memory is inside the total above.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpInterfaceScale: How large every panel draws, for a dense or a distant screen.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpInUse: Frames held on the card, ready to show without compositing.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpInUse2: Frames on disk, one promotion away from playing.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpLanguage: What Lumit is written in. Translations come from volunteers, so a new language may be part English at first.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpMotion: How much controls animate as they change.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpNotHeldByAnyCache: The process, less every store above that is inside it — which on this machine includes the frames on the card. A large number here is not a cache to shrink: it is memory nothing in this window is counting, and it is worth reporting.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpNowhereToPark: Nowhere: this machine has no folder Lumit may write to.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpOpenMediaDecoders: One per footage item in play. Each holds buffers of its own that no budget here covers.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpPanelLayout: Return every panel to its default place and size.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpPasteLayersAtTheirOriginal: A pasted layer keeps the timecode it was copied at, instead of starting at the playhead. For rebuilding the same moment in a second composition; leave it off for the everyday "put one here". Effects always paste with their first keyframe at the playhead, whichever way this is set.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpPlayheadStaysWherePlaybackSt: Leave the playhead on the frame that was on screen when playback stopped, instead of putting it back where playing started. Dragging the ruler while playing always stops and follows the pointer, whichever way this is set.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpQualityTier: What the realtime controller has settled on.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpRetimeOpensToVelocity: The Retime graph opens showing playback speed per cent — one point per keyframe, dragged up to speed up and below zero to reverse — instead of which moment of the source is showing.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpRetimeValuesInSeconds: The Retime row shows which moment of the source is playing as a number of seconds, instead of as a timecode in the same HH:MM:SS:FF form as every other time in the editor. Seconds can say a position between two frames; a timecode cannot.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpScopeEverywhere: Every project that has not been given a place of its own.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpScopeThisProject: Saved inside this project, so it travels with a copy of it.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpShapeEasesInAPopup: The graph editor's Easing button opens the shape editor in a small floating box instead of the Easing panel. The box closes whenever you click outside it — and choosing different keyframes is a click outside — so one drawn shape can only be tried on the selection that was live when it opened. Turn it on to save the screen space.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpShowTheToneMapButton: Put the tone map button on the Viewer bar. Tone mapping folds a picture brighter than the screen can show back into what it can, so the detail up there can be seen while you work — it is a way of looking, and it never reaches an export. Off unless you ask for it.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpSmoothThePictureWhenZoomed: Off, a pixel magnified past 1:1 stays a square, which is what you zoom in to see. On, the picture is blended between pixels — softer, and easier on the eye when the zoom is for framing rather than for inspecting.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpSurroundTakesThemeColours: Off, the area around the picture is a neutral grey — a grade cannot be judged against a tinted surround. On, it matches the rest of the shell.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpThisProcess: What the system says Lumit is holding, all in — the number Activity Monitor and Task Manager show.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpTransformInEffectControls: Repeat the layer's Transform rows above its effects. The Timeline already shows them when a layer is twirled open.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpUseThemeColours: Off, a scope reads on the standard near-black graticule whatever the chrome — which is how a signal is measured. On, it takes the theme's colours instead.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpVideoArrivesAsASequence: Video and image sequences added to a composition become a Sequence layer, which can be cut into clips on its own row. Still images are never wrapped.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpVramBudget: How much video memory finished frames may hold, of the {total} on the card.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpWaveformsRiseFromTheBottom: A waveform stands on the floor of its row instead of being centred about silence, each column reaching up by how far the sound swung either way. Half of a centred wave is a mirror of the other half, so this spends the whole row on the half that says something — useful in a short row. Applies to the single wave and the frequency stack alike.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpWaveformsShowTheFrequencySta: A layer's waveform draws as three stacked waves — bass, middle and treble — instead of one. A loud passage is a solid block on a single wave whichever instrument is playing; the stack shows the kick apart from the hats, so a cut can be aimed at either. Turn it off for one plain wave.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpWhenTheMachineCannotKeep: Adaptive keeps time and softens the picture; every frame keeps the picture and takes the time it needs.
zh_Hant.settingsHelpYourThemes: Duplicate one to change it without losing the original, or send one to somebody as a file.
